hook: You forget words mid-sentence — the word is right there, and then it isn't
topic: Cortisol suppression of prefrontal cortex and working memory
body:
**You're mid-sentence. The word you need is — you can almost feel the shape of it. And then it's gone. And this is happening multiple times a day.**

That experience has a specific neurological explanation, and it is not what most people fear it is.

When cortisol is chronically elevated — which happens when you're under sustained pressure, sleeping poorly, or running on a background hum of low-grade stress — it directly suppresses activity in the prefrontal cortex. That is the region responsible for working memory. The temporary mental workspace where you hold information mid-thought, mid-sentence.

When that system is degraded, words don't disappear because your vocabulary has shrunk. They disappear because the workspace where you were holding them just collapsed.

This is why the word-retrieval problem clusters with stress, poor sleep, and cognitive overload. They share a mechanism: cortisol suppression of the same neural region.

The fix is not verbal exercises. The fix is addressing the cortisol load. I'll explain how.
